core.title: Give every user/system flow a typed kebab-case identity
core.given: The change set contains a user/system flow definition document: a plan artifact whose purpose is to define one user/system flow (its own identity, title and contents), wherever it currently sits. Files that only reference user/system flows, and non-user/system-flow auxiliary files, are not user/system flow documents.
core.when: the planner creates, edits, renames or moves it, or changes its identity, title or file location
core.then: Set the user/system flow's identity to the stack's typed user/system flow URN, with both the subject and the descriptive-name segments in kebab-case.
prefer: Mandatory, not optional: store the user/system flow document flat at the stack's plan-item location for user/system flows, with the filename taken from the user/system flow identity.
Mandatory, not optional: write the title in Title Case.
avoid: Untyped identities missing the user/system flow URN's type prefix or its subject segment.
camelCase, snake_case, spaces or uppercase in the subject or descriptive name.
Titles not in Title Case (e.g. lowercase or a copied kebab-case identity).
Nesting the user/system flow document in subdirectories below its plan-item location, placing user/system flow documents outside it, or a filename that differs from the user/system flow identity.
Renaming or adding user/system flow identity fields to README, registry or other non-user/system-flow files.
core.why: A single typed, predictable identity gives each user/system flow one identity from which its file path and references can be derived mechanically.
evidence: Every user/system flow definition document sits flat at the stack's plan-item location for user/system flows (no subdirectories, none elsewhere) and its basename equals its user/system flow identity.
Each user/system flow identity matches the stack's typed user/system flow URN with both segments kebab-case.
verification: Identity check: every user/system flow definition document's identity matches the stack's user/system flow URN shape (type prefix, subject segment, descriptive-name segment) with both segments kebab-case; the concrete matcher (e.g. a regular expression) belongs to the realization.
Title check: every user/system flow title is Title Case.

File check: every user/system flow definition document sits flat at the stack's plan-item location for user/system flows, with basename equal to its identity — no subdirectories below it, none outside it.
One check covers the user/system flow identity, the title and the file naming together; the realization registers these under a single term id.

Candidate discovery belongs to the check: it scans plan artifacts anywhere under the plan root (including nested subdirectories of the user/system-flow-document location); a candidate is a plan artifact that declares its own user/system flow identity per the stack's URN-declaration syntax; the check confirms the candidate's purpose is to define one user/system flow before applying the checks; files of other kinds and files that only reference user/system flow identities are skipped.
The rule declares no exceptions: the naming invariants hold for the whole document on every covered operation.

facts.note: Discovery signal only: plan artifacts under the plan root — in the user/system-flow-document location (including nested subdirectories) or elsewhere under the plan root — are candidates. Path membership alone does not make a file a user/system flow document; README, notes and other non-user/system-flow auxiliary files in that location are out of scope.
User/system flow documents are files of the stack's plan-artifact kind; files of other kinds (e.g. a README) are never user/system flow documents.
Any change to a user/system flow document, including edits to non-identity fields; the naming invariants hold for the whole document.
Planning tasks that mention defining, editing, renaming or moving a user/system flow or its identity; the stack's local name for the identity field comes from the profile's URN-declaration syntax.

values: a candidate plan artifact declares its own user/system flow identity
facts.note: Content observer to surface candidates (including user/system flow documents misplaced outside or nested within the user/system-flow-document location). A declared identity is a discovery signal, not proof: registries or files that merely reference user/system flow identities are not user/system flow documents.
Final classification: the candidate's purpose is to define one user/system flow (its own identity, title and contents), as opposed to an auxiliary, registry or reference-only file.

fires: Planner creates a new user/system flow definition document.
Planner edits any field of an existing user/system flow definition document, including only its title or only its product capability list.
Planner renames a user/system flow, changes its identity, or moves its definition file.
A user/system flow definition document sits in a subdirectory below its plan-item location, outside it, or under a filename that differs from its identity.
doesNotFire: Editing a README, notes or other non-user/system-flow auxiliary file in the user/system-flow-document location.
Editing a registry or other plan artifact that only references user/system flow identities without defining a user/system flow.
Editing product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES or acceptances without creating, editing or moving any user/system flow definition document.
Code or doc changes that contain no user/system flow definition document.

profileRequirements.bunValue: user-system-flow:{subject}:{descriptive-name}, with both subject and descriptive name in kebab-case

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of plan artifacts; the discovery scan covers plan artifacts anywhere under it, so user/system flow documents misplaced outside or nested within the user/system-flow-document location are still found.

Path of one plan artifact under the plan root, used per its documented general meaning; for this rule it is the flat location and filename pattern of the user/system flow definition document, with the filename taken from the user/system flow identity.

How a plan artifact declares its own URN, used per its documented general meaning; for a user/system flow document this declaration is the content observer's discovery signal for candidate user/system flow documents.

neutralityNotes: Everything concrete was routed to the profile: the typed identity shape (urn.user-system-flow), the discovery scan root (roots.plan), the plan-artifact file kind (suffix.plan_artifact), the user/system flow document's path (layout.plan_item, used for its documented general meaning 'path of one plan artifact under the plan root' — the stack's value for the user/system flow document is plan/_user_system_flows/{user_system_flow_id}.yaml) and the user/system flow identity declaration syntax (urn.declaration, 'how a plan artifact declares its own URN' — here a top-level user_system_flow_id field). No new profile keys are needed: the vocabulary's general plan-artifact keys cover the user/system flow case, and their DESIRED OUTCOME examples are illustrative rather than exclusive assignments. kebab-case and Title Case are kept in the core as stack-neutral casing conventions (they bind to no runtime, framework or language). 'planner', 'user/system flow', 'product capability' and 'DESIRED OUTCOME' are treated as neutral ATDD plan vocabulary rather than stack names. The exact detector regex and the term id user_system_flow_naming have no neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly; the core's verification describes the same checks generically. Facts carry a 'note' field (beyond the minimal schema) to preserve the discovery-signal-only scoping semantics of the frozen rewrite.
